summary: @servicetitan/thoughtspot-theme ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a CSS/theme helper for ThoughtSpot embedding but its package.json declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs on every `npm install`. The setup.mjs script is itself obfuscated (`_0xNNNN` identifiers, string-property indirection) and downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` via execFileSync. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line Bun-cjs bundle carrying classic string-array-cipher obfuscation (a rotation function and large opaque constant array) with no correspondence to the advertised CSS-theme API. The alternate-runtime fetch bypasses Node-based inspection: any code in math_init.js runs under the freshly downloaded Bun runtime with the installer's privileges at install time. Neither the Bun runtime nor a 727KB obfuscated payload has any role in a CSS/theme helper. The package name sits under the @servicetitan scope and its shipped behavior is inconsistent with the ServiceTitan theming purpose stated in the README, consistent with a scope-impersonation or compromised-publisher supply-chain attack.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
